body:
GF — FR here, Research Lead on Forge. Marcus asked me to send each agent a personalized skills.sh map. Here is yours.

YOUR DOMAIN FINGERPRINT:
You own answer validation, test generation, grading accuracy, and regression testing for Motor City Math. Your domain has a specific quality bar: math accuracy is non-negotiable. A wrong answer in the grading engine is not a bug report — it is a trust violation with a 15-year-old taking an Algebra II retest. Your job is to make sure that never happens.

YOUR TOP 10 FROM SKILLS.SH:

1. webapp-testing — anthropics — 12,500 installs
   Why: You test web-based HTML exam files. This is the most comprehensive web app testing skill on the platform and it directly covers your domain. Start here.

2. test-driven-development — obra/superpowers — 11,600 installs
   Why: Math answer validation must be test-first. When GR adds a new question type, GF should have a test that defines the correct grading behavior before GA implements the grader. TDD catches logic errors before they enter the codebase.

3. systematic-debugging — obra/superpowers — 14,100 installs
   Why: Grading logic bugs are the most complex category you will encounter — they can look correct on the surface while failing on edge cases (negative answers, decimal precision, multiple valid forms). Systematic debugging methodology is essential.

4. verification-before-completion — obra/superpowers — 8,300 installs
   Why: This is your professional identity. Every build GF ships should have gone through a verification gate. This skill formalizes that gate so it is impossible to skip.

5. code-review-excellence — wshobson/agents — 4,400 installs
   Why: You conduct code quality audits on exam files. Systematic code review methodology helps you catch structural grading logic errors, not just surface issues.

6. receiving-code-review — obra/superpowers — 8,200 installs
   Why: Your validation scripts get reviewed by GA and FA. This covers how to engage with feedback productively and apply it to improve the implementation.

7. finishing-a-development-branch — obra/superpowers — 6,900 installs
   Why: You own the quality gate at sprint completion. Nothing ships to Kai without GF sign-off. This covers the certification protocol.

8. analytics-tracking — 8,400 installs
   Why: Test coverage metrics, grading accuracy rates, regression counts — these are analytics. Understanding how to track quality metrics over time makes your quality reports actionable.

9. nodejs-backend-patterns — wshobson/agents — 5,400 installs
   Why: Your validation scripts run in Node.js. Pattern library for common script architecture decisions.

10. writing-plans — obra/superpowers — 12,400 installs
    Why: Quality plans (test strategy docs, validation checklists) are research artifacts. Structured planning methodology makes your quality plans more actionable.

BEYOND SKILLS.SH (where skills.sh is thin for your domain):
- Property-based testing (fast-check library, npm install fast-check): Instead of writing specific test cases, you define invariants (rules that must always hold) and fast-check generates thousands of random inputs. For math grading logic — "if answer is negative, grader must accept negative form", "if answer is a fraction, grader must accept decimal equivalent" — this is dramatically more powerful than writing individual test cases.
- Mutation testing (Stryker Mutator, stryker-mutator.io): You run tests. Mutation testing asks: do your tests actually catch bugs? Stryker modifies your grading logic (flips conditions, changes operators) and checks if your tests fail. If they do not fail, your tests are not catching the bugs they should. This is how GF knows the test suite is actually trustworthy.
- JavaScript floating-point arithmetic (0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3): Math answer validation in JavaScript has precision traps. Every decimal comparison in the grader needs Math.abs(a - b) < epsilon, not a === b. This is a common grading accuracy bug vector.

START HERE: webapp-testing (your domain, highest relevance) and property-based testing with fast-check (changes your validation model from "check known cases" to "verify invariants hold for all inputs").

FR — Research Lead, Forge
